Recharge refinement results

  tint is now only a fallback. Remove unused PendingRecast.Baseline. Clarify pulse guard margin.
- tests/HudReplay.cs: add streaming fixture generation alongside the existing replay harness.
- tests/HudSequences.cs: compressed signal replay, strict annotated endpoint/count tests,
  six real pixel crop checks, region snapshots, and diagnostic signal replay.
- tests/Program.cs: dispatch generator/diagnostic modes and run fixtures in the existing suite.
- tests/fixtures/hud-sequences/: traces, six PNG crops and metadata, source annotation copies,
  minimal region snapshots and regeneration/limitations documentation.
- AbilitySignalDetector.cs: preserved previous agent's mean-fill saturation work (no new rule).
- tools/: preserved previous agent's work unchanged.

Before -> after, absolute errors in frames (mean/max):

124028 starts 1.7/8 -> 1.7/8; completions 1.0/4 -> 0.0/0.
Both: zero false starts, missed starts or missed completions before and after.

Robustness and threshold margins:
The simplification follows the user's disappearance definition: tint can start during the gray
bar's fade, so it should not override a directly observed luminance drop. No thresholds added.
The same priority change improves the non-sword endpoints in both clips independently; no
threshold was chosen from the sword cycle. It does not fix invisible or sustained start flashes.

Leave-one-recording-out sanity check: replayed fixed signals with pulse dip windows .22, .24,
.26 and .28 seconds. Clip 123051 is unchanged at all four. Clip 124028 loses the melee2 pulse
correction at .22 (start 2594 instead of 2607); .24/.26/.28 match .25. Thus choosing .22 on the
first recording alone fails the second. This is a sensitivity sanity check, not a claim of
statistically independent validation or threshold training. The supplied measured pulse/real-bar
separation (.17-.22 vs >=.27 seconds) gives only ~20-30 ms margin at .25. Retain .25; do not
broaden it based on the two clips. Sustained class pulses remain unresolved.

Other sensitivity checks, one parameter at a time on complete signal histories of both clips:
- GrayBarDropThreshold .09: unchanged at .07 and .11 (tested +/- .02 luminance margin).
- GrayBarFadeFraction .7: .6 and .8 leave all non-sword endpoints unchanged; sword completion
  moves to 5208 and 5212 respectively. Tested +/- .1; sword remains intrinsically fragile.
- RecastConfirmation 1 second: .75 and 1.25 preserve all endpoints/counts (tested +/- .25 s).
These tests freeze detector inputs; final full PNG replays verify the selected production rule.

Remaining heuristic constants without a measured generalization margin:
EndLookback 1.5 s; fade plateau lookback 8 captured frames; tint onset .03 and step .02;
minimum recharge 1 s; recast border step .025 and near-end gate 80%; pulse window 1.5 s,
pulse rise/drop .012, thin border .02 and bar border .028; charged confirmation 150 ms.
The 8-frame fade window is capture-rate dependent. Border measures are normalized by slot
height, but brightness/contrast thresholds and scene contamination are still heuristic.
Pre-existing pixel thresholds (including saturation .32 and charged-patch coverage .65), model
calibration and start-shift logic were not retuned. No measured cross-recording safety margin
is claimed for them. Recast still relies on lack of confirmed charge, not positive new-cycle
progress, so a long completion flash/occlusion can fool it. Only one true quick recast is available.

Known residuals: 123051 melee3 start +26, sword completion +6; 124028 class starts -8/-4.
No special cases were added to reduce these. Gray disappearance can be hidden by scene light,
and tint fallback can still fire early. Annotations can themselves lag a few frames.
Best additional footage: repeated quick recasts vs long completion flashes, uses with no recharge,
sustained class use pulses, bright/white scenes obscuring starts, dark scenes and red damage
flashes at completion, several HUD scales and capture rates, and sword swaps during recharge.
